title: Balance playtest: ability distribution and tuning
description: Play 10+ full games with all abilities active. Tune: (1) which Suit+Rank combos carry which abilities, (2) ability parameters (Extra Draw count, Double Trouble extra attack count), (3) overall fun — do abilities create interesting decisions or just noise? Track: how often each ability is activated vs played normally, which abilities feel overpowered or useless, whether the game still feels like Durak underneath.

notes: 200-game balance results: P0=101 P1=99 wins (balanced). All 6 abilities used: TrumpChanger 1.0/game, ExtraDraw 1.68, Blocker 1.86, DoubleTrouble 1.84, DoubleDefense 1.14, SeizeInitiative 1.0. 6-11 abilities/game, 0 stalls. Blocker/DoubleTrouble are most aggressive (greedy AI always activates). DeckConfig distribution (10 of 36 cards with abilities) looks good. Human playtest needed for subjective feel.

title: Implement Tier 1 abilities: Trump Changer + Extra Draw
description: Two simple state-mutation abilities. Trump Changer: when activated, changes Engine.Trump to the played card's suit. Once per game (set a flag). Extra Draw: when activated during attack, forces the defender to draw 2 cards from the deck before the defense phase begins. Both abilities consume the card (it goes to discard, not to the bout as an attack/defense).
design: Each ability is a static handler method in a new Abilities class, called by the engine when the player chooses 'ability'. Trump Changer fires a new OnTrumpChanged event so the HUD updates. Extra Draw calls the existing DrawTo mechanism but with an incremented target.
acceptance_criteria: Trump Changer changes the trump suit visually and mechanically. Extra Draw forces 2 cards drawn. Both work for human and AI. Engine smoke test still passes.
close_reason: Trump Changer and Extra Draw implemented in GameEngine (ValidateAbility + ApplyAbility dispatch). GameManager wired: OnTrumpChanged refreshes HUD/highlights, ability cards stay clickable even when not normally playable. Validated, 50-game smoke test passes.

title: Engine: ability choice micro-phase
description: When a player plays a card that has an ability, the engine must let them choose: play normally or activate the ability. Add a new Phase or callback pattern so the UI can present a modal and the AI can compute. IPlayerController gets a RequestAbilityChoice method or the engine fires an OnAbilityChoice event. The engine waits for the choice before resolving the play. If the player chooses 'normal', the existing TryAttack/TryDefend path runs unchanged. If 'ability', the engine calls the ability handler instead.
design: Keep the engine synchronous for AI (AI returns the choice immediately) and event-driven for humans (UI shows modal, player clicks, callback resolves). Avoid adding a new Phase enum value if possible — use a pending-choice flag on the engine instead, so the GameLoop knows to wait.
acceptance_criteria: Playing an ability card triggers a choice. Choosing 'normal' behaves identically to the current flow. Choosing 'ability' is a no-op stub for now (individual ability handlers come in later tasks).
close_reason: Engine.TryUseAbility stub added (validates player/phase/ability, consumes card to discard, fires OnAbilityUsed). Scene rebuilt.

title: GameEngine fires Played events before updating Phase, freezing UI
description: Repro: human attacks 8d, AI defends with 9d. HUD stays at 'Knave defends', End bout disabled, no card highlights, even though the bout is fully defended and Phase should now be Attack. Cause: TryAttack and TryDefend invoke their events before assigning Phase, so GameManager.OnDefensePlayed runs UpdateHud+ApplyHighlightForPhase against the still-Defense Phase. After the engine sets Phase=Attack, no event fires to refresh the UI, so the HUD stays stuck. Fix: assign Phase BEFORE firing the event in both TryAttack (Phase=Defense) and TryDefend (Phase=Attack).
close_reason: Fixed: in TryAttack and TryDefend, Phase is now assigned BEFORE the OnAttackPlayed/OnDefensePlayed event fires, so synchronous handlers (UpdateHud, ApplyHighlightForPhase) see the new Phase. Engine smoke test still passes 50/50 games with identical numbers.

title: AI ability evaluation policy
description: Extend AIPlayer to decide when to activate abilities vs play cards normally. Heuristics per ability: Trump Changer — activate when holding 3+ cards of the new suit and few of the current trump. Extra Draw — activate when defender has a small hand and deck is large (maximize long-term damage). Blocker — activate when the bout has 2+ attacks and defender wants to stop pile-on. Seize Initiative — activate when losing initiative would be costly (e.g., opponent has few cards). Double Trouble — activate when holding a card that doesn't match bout ranks (the free attack). Double Defense — activate when facing 2+ undefended attacks and the card can cover both.
design: Add an EvaluateAbilityUse method to AIPlayer that returns bool (use ability or play normally). Called by the ability choice callback. Start with simple heuristics; can be tuned during balance testing.
acceptance_criteria: AI uses abilities in reasonable situations. AI does not waste abilities when playing normally would be better. No frozen states when AI has ability cards.
close_reason: AI uses all 6 abilities with heuristics: TrumpChanger when 3+ of new suit, ExtraDraw when deck>=6, Blocker when 2+ attacks, DoubleTrouble when off-rank cards exist, DoubleDefense when can cover 2 slots, SeizeInitiative in defense. GameLoop pumps on ability use. Smoke test: 0 stalls, 11.9 avg turns (abilities shorten games).

design: Ability badge: small colored bar at the bottom of the card face with abbreviated ability name. Modal: a simple Canvas overlay centered on screen, similar to the GameOver panel. Tooltip: a floating TMP_Text that follows the cursor.

title: Implement Tier 2 abilities: Blocker, Seize Initiative, Double Trouble, Double Defense
description: Four abilities that modify bout rules. The Blocker (defense): sets a flag on the bout preventing the attacker from adding more cards this bout. Seize Initiative (either phase): sets a flag so the activating player becomes attacker after bout resolves, regardless of defense outcome. Double Trouble (attack): grants one additional attack this bout that ignores the rank-match constraint. Double Defense (defense): the played card covers the current undefended slot AND the next one, if both attacks can be beaten by this card's rank or suit.
design: Bout gets new flags: AttacksCapped (for Blocker), and a slot for 'double defense covers two'. GameEngine.ResolveBout checks a SeizeInitiative override for attacker selection. Double Trouble temporarily relaxes CanAttackWith for one play. These are the most complex abilities — each modifies a different part of the rules pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: All four abilities function correctly for human and AI. Edge cases tested: Blocker when attacker has no follow-ups (no-op), Double Defense when only one attack exists (covers just one), Seize Initiative when activator already would have been attacker (no-op), Double Trouble when no legal follow-up rank exists (the extra attack can be any rank).
close_reason: All 4 Tier 2 abilities implemented. Blocker: caps attacks via Bout.AttacksCapped. Seize Initiative: overrides attacker selection in ResolveBout. Double Trouble: rank bypass flag consumed on next TryAttack. Double Defense: card defends first slot + auto-defends second slot. Bout extended with AutoDefend/AttacksCapped. Validated, smoke test passes.

value: unity-mcp bridge (com.unity.ai.assistant relay) drops when Unity does a domain reload (Play mode entry while compiling, or RunCommand crashes inside Unity). Doesn't auto-recover; requires /mcp reload in Claude Code. Workaround: wait for compile to fully finish before pressing Play. Time penalty per drop: ~30 seconds + user interaction.

Wits&Fools engine smoke test: menu 'Wits and Fools/Smoke Test/Play 50 Games (Greedy AIs)' or via Unity_ManageMenuItem. Runs 50 deterministic games with greedy AIs vs each other. Healthy result: 0 stalls (safety cap), roughly balanced wins, avg ~13 turns/game. Prints to Unity console — read with FilterText='Smoke Test'.

Wits&Fools: GameLoop initially Pumped() synchronously inside OnAttackPlayed handler, which caused AI to act before GameManager's visual handler ran (subscriber order). Refactored to GameLoop.Tick() called per-frame from GameManager.Update; AI ticks delayed by AiThinkSeconds for deliberate pacing. Avoids re-entering engine inside its own events.

RunManager.StartAutoRun() drives complete roguelike runs without UI interaction. Press R to toggle during non-match phases. Uses Time.timeScale=20 and AiThinkSeconds=0.02f for fast execution. Auto-selects map nodes (Match > Elite > Rest > Rumor > Shop priority). GameManager.SetAutoPlay(true) enables match auto-play. Stall detection in GameManager.Update forces TryEat after 100 stalled frames.
